## T3.1: how we work

::: {.steps}
::: {.step}
<b>Map stakeholders</b><br>For each pilot: community managers, DSO staff, building operators, regulators.
:::
::: {.step}
<b>Co-design workshops</b><br>Personas and user journeys, including non-expert users.
:::
::: {.step}
<b>Inventory the data</b><br>Source, owner, format, access conditions, privacy class.
:::
::: {.step}
<b>Scope the semantics</b><br>Map each item to IEC CIM or PECO and list the gaps.
:::
::: {.step}
<b>Consolidate</b><br>One requirements register with IDs and priorities.
:::
::: {.step}
<b>Review</b><br>Pilot partners first, then the advisory board (MSAB).
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Key sentence: the data inventory and the semantic gap list are what partners can start on this month.
The proposal assumes CIM and PECO are expressive enough. Targeted expert interviews in step 4 test that assumption.
:::

## Three use cases, three blueprints

::: {.lead}
AIT introduced the use cases this afternoon. This is what each blueprint adds.
:::

::: {.cols}
::: {.col .ecp}
<span class="tag">ECP, Austria and Italy</span>

Planning dialogue for non-experts: PV, storage, community scope, viability.

The blueprint settles:

- which public and community data feed it
- how national incentives become rules
:::
::: {.col .edcr}
<span class="tag">EDCR, Sweden and France</span>

Operator decision support, in shadow mode.

The blueprint settles:

- which events it covers
- which DSO-informed grid constraints apply
- what the operator sees and can override
:::
::: {.col .esla}
<span class="tag">ESLA, Austria and France</span>

Automated lifecycle of an energy service.

The blueprint settles:

- the reference service to automate
- which steps run without a human
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Each pilot host writes the first draft of its own blueprint from a common template. KTH consolidates.
Likely question: what does the French side need to provide? The proposal describes the Swedish EDCR in most detail, so France needs the most clarifying.
:::

## T3.2: from targets to baselines

::: {.lead}
The KPIs were shown in the overview. D3.2 makes each one measurable.
:::

| Objective | Target | D3.2 adds |
|:--|:--|:--|
| O1 Orchestration | 30 to 50% less manual effort | Baseline effort, definition of "without human intervention" |
| O2 Federation | Under 2 s for 90% of queries | Test queries and the onboarding baseline |
| O3 Explainability | 85% operator acceptance | Survey instrument, definition of the Trust-Score |
| O4 Demonstration | Planning under 21 days | Baselines per pilot, shadow-mode protocol |

::: {.notes}
Key sentence: we keep the proposal's targets and make each one measurable. The full KPI list is in the backup.
Every KPI needs a formula, a unit, a baseline, a data source, an owner and a tolerance.
Likely question: who sets the baseline? The pilot host measures it, KTH defines how.
:::

## T3.3: the architecture

::: {.blocks}
::: {.row}
::: {.blk .top}
<b>ECP toolbox</b>chat and scenario dashboard
:::
::: {.blk .top}
<b>EDCR toolbox</b>operator dashboard
:::
::: {.blk .top}
<b>ESLA toolbox</b>notebooks and workflow queue
:::
:::
::: {.row}
::: {.blk}
<b>Agent orchestration</b>central orchestrator, hierarchical task planning, fallback
:::
::: {.blk}
<b>Federated semantic layer</b>Semantic API, SPARQL, CIM and PECO, data stays at source
:::
::: {.blk}
<b>Explainability and trust</b>explanations, regulatory guardrails, human feedback
:::
:::
::: {.row}
::: {.blk .base}
<b>Physical guardrail</b>power-flow check of every control recommendation, target under 100 ms
:::
::: {.blk .base}
<b>Audit and security</b>traceability, manual override, role-based access
:::
:::
:::

::: {.callout}
Still open: where connectors run, identity between agents, what may leave a site, the deployment target.
:::

::: {.notes}
The building blocks come straight from the proposal. T3.3 turns them into interfaces and decisions, one decision record each.
Likely question: which LLM? Open. The proposal prefers small language models and federated inference to limit footprint.
:::

## How we decide

::: {.lead}
Project governance comes from WP1 this afternoon. These rules belong to WP3.
:::

::: {.flow}
::: {.node}
<b>Draft</b>task partners write
:::
<div class="arrow"></div>
::: {.node}
<b>Internal review</b>two partners who did not write it
:::
<div class="arrow"></div>
::: {.node}
<b>MSAB review</b>D3.1 and D3.2
:::
<div class="arrow"></div>
::: {.node .hot}
<b>Sign-off</b>pilot hosts, M09
:::
:::

- Every requirement gets an ID in one register, kept in the project workspace.
- After M09, a change needs a request that states its effect on WP4, WP5 and WP6.
- Disagreements go to the technical board.

::: {.notes}
All of this is a proposal. Small clarifications after the freeze do not need a request.
Likely question: who is in the MSAB? The nominations were collected in the 16:00 session. WP3 asks only for the first meeting date.
:::

## Backup: the proposal's KPIs {.smaller}

| Objective | KPI | Verification in the proposal |
|:--|:--|:--|
| O1 | 30 to 50% less manual engineering effort | Manual against agentic benchmark in WP6 |
| O1 | Over 90% task success without human intervention | Logs from stress tests |
| O1 | 15 to 20% local peak load reduction | Functional tests of orchestration |
| O2 | Semantic mapping under 500 ms per data point | Benchmark of the Semantic API (T5.2) |
| O2 | Cross-site queries under 2 s for 90% of requests | Federated SPARQL tests |
| O2 | At least 50% less data onboarding time | Cross-site reuse in the pilots |
| O3 | 100% audit trail for high-risk decisions | AI Act self-assessment (T1.2), rule-based checks |
| O3 | 85% operator acceptance, transparency at least 4 of 5 | Pilot surveys |
| O3 | Over 80% of operators confirm the AI logic | Pilot surveys |
| O4 | Assessment time from about 3 months to under 21 days | KPI logging in the pilots |
| O4 | DSO pre-assessment under 4 hours (baseline 40 man-hours) | KPI logging in the pilots |
| O4 | Hosting capacity up 10 to 20%, congestion hours down 25 to 40% | Independent verification, TRL assessment |

## Backup: architecture questions to close {.smaller}

| Topic | Questions |
|:--|:--|
| Layers | Which modules exist, what does each own, which interfaces are public? |
| Agent contracts | Registration, input and output schemas, error envelope, versioning |
| Data access | Where do connectors run? How are schema changes handled? Which SPARQL features are required? |
| Security | Authentication between agents and external systems, access model, secrets, network zones at pilot sites |
| Data sovereignty | What may leave a site? How is GDPR handled for building and consumption data? |
| Human oversight | Where do recommendations wait for approval? How are overrides logged and fed back? |
| Traceability | What the audit logger records, how long, who can read it |
| Deployment | Cloud-native target, sizing for 10 communities and 100 concurrent agents, edge devices at pilots |
| LLM strategy | Which models, where hosted, how recommendations are grounded in grid data |
| Licensing | Which components are open (Apache 2.0, Zenodo) and which stay proprietary |

## Backup: risks for WP3 {.smaller}

| Risk | Mitigation |
|:--|:--|
| Semantic incompatibility between pilot sites | Use CIM and SAREF, start mapping early, expert interviews in the first phase |
| Unstable access to DSO or community data | Data access agreements early, access status in the data inventory, synthetic data as fallback |
| Explanations too technical for non-experts | Define "understandable" with users in the co-creation workshops |
| Late or unclear requirements delay WP4 and WP5 | Drafts shared from M05, freeze at M09, traceability matrix |
| KPIs too vague to measure in WP6 | Baseline, formula and data source for every KPI in D3.2 |
| Little partner time in M01 to M09 | Short sessions, templates prepared by KTH, workshops grouped |
